newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica to sell consumer finance unit.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica to sell consumer finance unit.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp. said Friday it plans to sell Security Pacific Financial Services, one of the nation's largest traditional consumer finance companies.

BankAmerica acquired the subsidiary in its 1992 merger with Security Pacific Corp. It provides home equity and other loans secured by real estate, as well as unsecured instalment loans and sales financing through retail merchants.
"As part of our on-going capital management strategy, we are looking at all business units," Michael O'Neill, BankAmerica's chief financial officer, said in a statement.
"We believe we can put the capital we have devoted to Security Pacific Financial Services to better use for our shareholders.
"At the same time, we believe the network and book of business that the company has developed will be valuable to a number of potential acquirers."

Security Pacific Financial has loan assets of about $1.4 billion, excluding its Executive and Professional business unit, which will not be sold. It operates its own network of 300 offices in 33 states.
BankAmerica, based in San Francisco, said it hopes to conclude the sale in the second half of 1997.
BankAmerica has hired Bear Stearns & Co. Inc. to advise it on the sale.
BankAmerica stock rose $2.875 to $121.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
